nodes.description: Gnb5 knockout mice show abnormal neuronal development in cerebellum and hippocampus and dysregulated neuronal gene expression. The authors propose that G-beta-5 regulates dendritic arborization or synapse formation. This has not been shown in patient tissue.
nodes.id: Abnormal Neuronal Development in Cerebellum and Hippocampus

evidence.reference_title: Knockout of G protein β5 impairs brain development and causes multiple neurologic abnormalities in mice.
evidence.snippet: We further show that Gβ5-deficient mice have abnormalities of neuronal development in cerebellum and hippocampus.

nodes.description: Electronegative dark-adapted ERG with absent rod responses and markedly reduced light-adapted responses, reported in a child homozygous for a null allele.

evidence.reference_title: Unique retinal signaling defect in GNB5-related disease.
evidence.snippet: The DA 3.0, 10.0 and 30.0 ERGs showed electronegative configuration regardless of the ISI

nodes.description: Variable expressivity within the original S81L family.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5 mutation causes a novel neuropsychiatric disorder featuring attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, severely impaired language development and normal cognition.
evidence.snippet: In an extended consanguineous family, we identified a novel neuropsychiatric phenotype characterized by severe speech impairment, variable expressivity of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and motor delay.

nodes.description: Parasympathomimetics should be used with extreme caution because they may cause asystole, and drugs that worsen bradycardia, especially beta blockers, are best avoided. This follows from the exaggerated cholinergic slowing of the pacemaker.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
evidence.snippet: Use parasympathomimetics with extreme caution because of the potential to cause asystole. It is best to avoid other drugs that can potentiate bradycardia, particularly beta blockers.

nodes.description: Sinus node dysfunction can progress, and a pacemaker has been implanted in young children with prolonged sinus pauses.

evidence.reference_title: Early pacing in a child with Lodder-Merla syndrome and progressive sinus node dysfunction: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Following multidisciplinary evaluation, an epicardial VVI pacemaker was implanted, after which cardiac rhythm stabilized with reliable suppression of prolonged pauses.

nodes.description: G-beta-5L with RGS9-1 switches off phototransduction in rods, and G-beta-5S with RGS11 and RGS7 works at the dendritic tips of ON-bipolar cells. Gnb5-/- mice have slow rod recovery, no ERG b-wave and fewer outer plexiform layer synapses. A child homozygous for the null allele p.Tyr344* had an electronegative dark-adapted ERG and absent rod responses, a combined defect resembling bradyopsia and rod ON-bipolar dysfunction.
nodes.id: Defective Retinal Photoreceptor and ON-Bipolar Cell Signaling

evidence.reference_title: Gbeta5 is required for normal light responses and morphology of retinal ON-bipolar cells.
evidence.snippet: We found that the electroretinogram of Gbeta5-/- mice lacks the b-wave component and that Gbeta5-S and RGS11 colocalize with Go alpha at the tips of the ON-bipolar cell dendrites.

evidence.reference_title: Defective retinal depolarizing bipolar cells in regulators of G protein signaling (RGS) 7 and 11 double null mice.
evidence.snippet: By characterizing a complete RGS7 and RGS11 double knock-out (711dKO) mouse line, we found that Gβ5S expression in the retinal outer plexiform layer is eliminated, as is the ERG b-wave.

evidence.reference_title: Unique retinal signaling defect in GNB5-related disease.
evidence.snippet: The observed phenotype is consistent with a dual retinal signaling defect reminiscent of features of bradyopsia and rod ON-bipolar dysfunction.

nodes.description: Acetylcholine released by the vagus nerve acts on m2 muscarinic receptors on pacemaker cells. The released G-beta-gamma opens the acetylcholine-activated potassium channel (I-K,ACh, a GIRK1/GIRK4 channel), which slows the heart. Without Gbeta5-R7 RGS the response is larger and lasts longer. In isogenic iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes homozygous for p.Ser81Leu, the carbachol-induced I-K,ACh current is larger and spontaneous beating slows more. A specific I-K,ACh blocker almost fully reversed this.
nodes.id: Enhanced Muscarinic IKACh Activation in Sinoatrial Node Cells

evidence.reference_title: Genetic variation in GNB5 causes bradycardia by augmenting the cholinergic response via increased acetylcholine-activated potassium current (I(K,ACh)).
evidence.snippet: Application of the specific I(KACh) blocker XEN-R0703 resulted in near-complete reversal of the phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: RGS6/Gβ5 complex accelerates IKACh gating kinetics in atrial myocytes and modulates parasympathetic regulation of heart rate.
evidence.snippet: The cardiac Rgs6/Gβ5 complex modulates the timing of parasympathetic influence on atrial myocytes and heart rate in mice.

nodes.description: The heart rate falls too far in response to vagal (cholinergic) input. In Gnb5-/- mice the resting heart rate was higher, but carbachol caused profound bradycardia and sinus arrhythmias were more frequent.
nodes.id: Exaggerated Parasympathetic Slowing of Heart Rate

evidence.reference_title: Inhibition of G-protein signalling in cardiac dysfunction of intellectual developmental disorder with cardiac arrhythmia (IDDCA) syndrome.
evidence.snippet: In contrast, Gnb5-/- mice exhibited profound bradycardia on treatment with carbachol, while sympathetic modulation of the cardiac stimulation was not altered.

evidence.reference_title: Inhibition of G-protein signalling in cardiac dysfunction of intellectual developmental disorder with cardiac arrhythmia (IDDCA) syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous Gnb5 loss resulted in significantly higher frequencies of sinus arrhythmias.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of GNB5-NDD is established in a proband with suggestive clinical findings and biallelic pathogenic variants in GNB5 identified by molecular genetic testing.

evidence.reference_title: IDDCA syndrome in a Chinese infant due to GNB5 biallelic mutations.
evidence.snippet: Whole-exome sequencing showed that the infant had two compound heterozygous variants, NM_016194:c.458G>A/p.Cys153Tyr and NM_016194:c.1032C>A/p.Tyr344*, in GNB5.

evidence.reference_title: Inheritance of c.628-6G>A GNB5 hypomorphic allele uncovers another challenge in the pathogenic prediction of genomic variants.
evidence.snippet: We studied a patient with a severe phenotype carrying two GNB5 variants: c.514delT from the unaffected heterozygous mother and c.628-6G>A from the unaffected homozygous father.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Phenotype in a Patient With Homozygous 15q21.2 Microdeletion Involving BCL2L10, GNB5, and MYO5C Genes, Resembling Infantile Developmental Disorder With Cardiac Arrhythmias (IDDCA).
evidence.snippet: We report the first case of a patient carrying a homozygous 15q21.2 microdeletion, encompassing GNB5 and the two contiguous genes BCL2L10 and MYO5C.

nodes.description: Biallelic GNB5 variants remove or reduce the G-beta-5 protein. Truncating alleles are loss-of-function. The p.Ser81Leu missense allele is hypomorphic: the mutant protein is poorly expressed. A deep intronic splice allele, c.628-6G>A, is also hypomorphic and gives about half the normal transcript.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5 Mutations Cause an Autosomal-Recessive Multisystem Syndrome with Sinus Bradycardia and Cognitive Disability.
evidence.snippet: We observed an association between the nature of the variants and clinical severity

evidence.reference_title: Inheritance of c.628-6G>A GNB5 hypomorphic allele uncovers another challenge in the pathogenic prediction of genomic variants.
evidence.snippet: Functional genomics studies showed that parents express 50% (nonsense-mediated decay, NMD) of the RNA/protein while the patient does not produce enough protein for normal development.

nodes.description: Present before seizure onset in the severe form, where development ultimately reaches profound impairment without regression.

evidence.reference_title: The epileptology of GNB5 encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: All nine had abnormal development prior to seizure onset and ultimately had profound impairment without regression.

nodes.description: Knockout mice lose all R7 RGS proteins. They have slow rod recovery and no ERG b-wave, impaired neurological development and hyperactivity, and profound carbachol-induced bradycardia with sinus arrhythmias. Resting heart rate is higher than in wild type, unlike patients.
CRISPR/Cas9-edited isogenic human iPSC lines, wild type, heterozygous or homozygous for p.Ser81Leu, differentiated into cardiomyocytes that express I-K,ACh.

G-beta-5 dimerizes with the R7 RGS proteins (RGS6, RGS7, RGS9, RGS11) through their G-gamma-like domain. The complexes are GTPase-accelerating proteins for Gi/o alpha subunits and switch off Gi/o-coupled receptor signaling. Knocking out Gnb5 in mice causes the whole Gbeta5-R7 family to be degraded.

evidence.reference_title: Targeted deletion of one or two copies of the G protein β subunit Gβ5 gene has distinct effects on body weight and behavior in mice.
evidence.snippet: Gβ5 is essential for stability of these complexes, so that its knockout (KO)causes degradation of the entire Gβ5-R7 family.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5 mutation causes a novel neuropsychiatric disorder featuring attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, severely impaired language development and normal cognition.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that the S81L mutant form of Gβ5 has significantly impaired activity in terminating responses that are elicited by dopamine.

molecular_functions: GTPase activator activity of R7 RGS proteins

evidence.reference_title: GNB5 mutation causes a novel neuropsychiatric disorder featuring attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, severely impaired language development and normal cognition.
evidence.snippet: In an extended consanguineous family, we identified a novel neuropsychiatric phenotype characterized by severe speech impairment, variable expressivity of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and motor delay.

nodes.description: In neurons the Gbeta5-R7 RGS complexes shut off Gi/o-coupled receptors, including dopamine D2-like, GABA-B and mu-opioid receptors. RGS7-Gbeta5 binds neuronal GIRK channels and sets the timing of GABA-B-GIRK inhibition. Without the complexes, inhibitory receptor signaling is stronger and lasts longer. In mice this goes with extreme hyperactivity, disturbed dopamine handling and motor learning deficits.
nodes.id: Prolonged Inhibitory GPCR Signaling in Neurons

evidence.reference_title: Gbeta5 recruits R7 RGS proteins to GIRK channels to regulate the timing of neuronal inhibitory signaling.
evidence.snippet: We found that mouse RGS7-Gbeta5 complexes bound to G protein-gated potassium channels and facilitated their functional coupling to GABA(B) receptors in neurons.

evidence.reference_title: Gβ5-RGS complexes are gatekeepers of hyperactivity involved in control of multiple neurotransmitter systems.
evidence.snippet: Neurochemical studies indicated that Gβ5-RGS-deficient mice had higher sensitivity of inhibitory GPCR signaling and deficits in basal levels, release, and reuptake of dopamine.

nodes.description: Sinoatrial node dysfunction with sinus pauses. It can progress and may need a pacemaker.

evidence.reference_title: Early pacing in a child with Lodder-Merla syndrome and progressive sinus node dysfunction: a case report.
evidence.snippet: In the largest cohort reported to date, SND was documented in 27 of 28 affected individuals.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic characterization and long-term management of severely affected siblings with intellectual developmental disorder with cardiac arrhythmia syndrome.
evidence.snippet: We report two brothers with severe global cognitive and motor delay, cortical visual impairment and sick sinus syndrome who were born to consanguineous parents.

nodes.description: Nearly universal across the spectrum, regardless of the neurodevelopmental phenotype, and often present from the neonatal period.

evidence.reference_title: GNB5-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder.
evidence.snippet: A unique and specific feature of GNB5-NDD – regardless of neurodevelopmental phenotype – is nearly universal bradycardia caused by sinoatrial node dysfunction (sick sinus syndrome).

evidence.reference_title: The epileptology of GNB5 encephalopathy.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic variants in GNB5 cause an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder with neonatal sinus bradycardia.
